findings.title: The new authority command still cannot execute the required terminal closeout sequence
findings.evidence: The CLI now exposes authority, but run_authority_execution stops after a Phase 8 curation projection, a Branch B successor/receipt, a limited Phase 12 probe, and authority_execution_summary.json. D1, D11, D13, and D15 are not accepted or consumed. The independent eligibility report, independent closeout review, owner seal, terminal branch disposition, sealed-successor closeout, final artifact manifest, and terminal hash seal still have only implementation-time schemas; repository search finds no post-authority producer for them.
findings.impact: The implementation cannot complete the plan's non-substitutable authority execution, terminal independent review, owner seal, and terminal hash sequence. The implementation-complete claim that all D1/D5-D16 option-capable code exists remains unsupported.
findings.required_action: Add a fail-closed post-authority closeout command that consumes the remaining decisions in the plan-defined order, validates the authority artifacts and distinct terminal reviewer eligibility, and write-once produces the final machine/artifact evidence, independent closeout, owner seal, branch disposition, and terminal hash.

findings.title: Naturalization tooling was adopted before D16 authorization and its manifest conceals the G0 preimage
findings.evidence: Both Naturalization runner/validator files, plus the two Naturalization test files, are staged additions and do not exist at G1 V0 HEAD 2a1741ce. Nevertheless _materialize_candidate_patch reads the already modified worktree, records preimage_state=present_and_D16_symbols_adopted, sets candidate_path=null and replacement_sha256 equal to that modified file, while the same manifest records D16_owner_authorization_consumed=false. The plan permits isolated candidate patches before D16 but forbids adopting current Naturalization tooling until D16 authorization.
findings.impact: The authorization boundary has already been crossed before owner D16, and the patch manifest cannot detect the real absent-at-G0 preimage or apply the authorized candidate after review.
findings.required_action: Preserve this attempt as failed. In a fresh attempt, keep D16 changes only as isolated candidate fragments with true G0 path/preimage identities; apply them to durable Naturalization tooling only after exact D16 authorization and reject absent/preimage-mismatch cases as specified.

findings.title: The Phase 2 probe validates file identities but not the actual consumer projection
findings.evidence: The authority path computes meaningful_profiles directly from pre-consumer automatic and curated rows. The no-render helper separately projects the successor facts, but the validator requires only food_semantic_proposition_count>0 and a syntactically 64-character inventory hash; it never compares the projected inventory exact set/count to approved propositions, checks required-axis coverage in that inventory, detects invented/dropped propositions, or derives the meaningful partitions from actual consumer output. A projection bug that drops any subset while leaving one proposition passes and the summary still asserts actual_phase2_no_render_identity_match=true.
findings.impact: Change 12 can PASS despite consumer projection loss, violating the actual-Phase-2-consumer, required-fact, compiler-invention-zero, and meaningful-partition validation boundary.
findings.required_action: Seal the expected approved proposition inventory, compare the actual Phase 2 inventory by exact proposition identity and content, validate required axes and invented/dropped counts, and compute partitions from the actual projected inventory before granting the Phase 12 predicate.

findings.title: D5 is recorded but its allow/deny Layer 4 behavior is not enforced
findings.evidence: validate_curated_rows accepts any non-empty strings in reviewed_source_set and has no source classification or D5 parameter. The authority input validator accepts either D5 option, then run_authority_execution merely copies the selected option into selected_workflow_options.json. Selecting deny_layer4_review_context does not reject a curated row whose reviewed source set is Layer 4, so the two advertised D5 implementations have identical behavior.
findings.impact: The implementation can consume forbidden review context under the deny option and does not meet the plan's requirement that all allowed owner-decision options be executable and disabled/fail-closed until selected.
findings.required_action: Bind reviewed sources to classified source identities and pass the selected D5 policy into curated-ledger validation, rejecting every Layer 4 source when deny is selected while preserving Layer 4 as human-review-only context when allow is selected.
